title_ar: الشيخ الددو يحاضر في القاهرة عن ملامح التغيير عند الخلفاء الراشدين
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures in Cairo on the Features of Change under the Rightly Guided Caliphs
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو اليوم الثلاثاء 03 يوليو 2012 بمدينة القاهرة عاصمة دولة مصر العربية محاضرة عن "ملامح التغيير عند الخلفاء الراشدين..عمر بن عبد العزيز نموذجا". و جاءت محاضر الشيخ خلال فعاليات اليوم الثالث من مؤتمر فور شباب العالمي الثالث..الذي ينظم هذا العام تحت شعار: "هندسة التغيير.. التكوين والأدوات" وبمشار كوكبة من العلماء وأصحاب الفكر والدعاة والمنشدين من بينهم المفكر الإسلامي راشد الغنوشي والدكتور محمد عماره والداعية الإسلامي سلمان العودة والمنشد عبد القادر قوزح. ويهدف المؤتمر الثالث لمنظمة افور شباب العالمية هذا العام إلى العمل على توفير بيئة علمية، ومفاهيم تغييرية و سرد تجارب عملية ووسائل مشروعة مدنية للتغيير الحضاري المنشود.
body_en:
Today, Tuesday 3 July 2012, in the city of Cairo, capital of the Arab Republic of Egypt, Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew delivered a lecture on "The Features of Change under the Rightly Guided Caliphs: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz as a Model".

The Sheikh's lecture came during the proceedings of the third day of the Third 4Shabab International Conference, organised this year under the banner "The Engineering of Change: Formation and Instruments", with the participation of a constellation of scholars, thinkers, callers to Islam and religious singers, among them the Islamic thinker Rached Ghannouchi, Dr Muhammad Imarah, the Islamic preacher Salman al-Awdah, and the singer Abd al-Qadir Quzah.

The third conference of the 4Shabab international organisation aims this year at working to provide a scholarly environment, concepts for change, the recounting of practical experiences, and legitimate civil means towards the civilisational change that is sought.

flags.arabic: ملامح التغيير عند الخلفاء الراشدين..عمر بن عبد العزيز نموذجا
flags.context: the lecture title; no content is given
options: render the title as served and record the difficulty
flags.note: The title places Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz as the exemplar of the Rightly Guided Caliphs. On the standard Sunni reckoning the Rightly Guided Caliphs are the four immediate successors of the Prophet, and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, an Umayyad caliph two generations later, is called the fifth by way of praise rather than by that count. Whether the Sheikh used the wider reckoning, or the news desk compressed a longer title, cannot be told: the record carries the title and not one word of the lecture. Nothing has been adjusted. The title is the whole of what the corpus holds on the subject and must not be displayed as if it were his argument.

flags.context: the conference's aims, as the news desk states them
options: means that are legitimate in the Sharia and civil in character
flags.note: mashrūʿ is 'legitimate' in the sense of sanctioned by the Sharia, from the same root as sharīʿah, and the pairing with مدني — civil, as against armed — makes the phrase a pointed disavowal of violent means, written in Cairo a year after the Egyptian revolution. 'Legitimate civil means' keeps both without spelling the disavowal out, which the source does not. Note that this is the conference's stated aim, not a statement by the Sheikh.

flags.arabic: و جاءت محاضر الشيخ ... وبمشار كوكبة من العلماء ... لمنظمة افور شباب
flags.context: three separate malformed words in one short record
options: read as محاضرة, بمشاركة and فور شباب respectively
flags.note: Three source typos: محاضر for محاضرة ('lecture'), بمشار for بمشاركة ('with the participation of'), and افور for فور in the organisation's name. All are preserved in body_ar and rendered on the obvious readings, per style guide section 11. The density of errors in this short record suggests it was posted in haste on the day.

options: performers of Islamic chant / the chanter
flags.note: A munshid performs anāshīd — Islamic vocal music, typically unaccompanied or with percussion only, a distinct genre from both song and Qur'anic recitation. No English word carries it: 'singer' loses the religious register and 'chanter' suggests liturgy. 'Religious singer' is used as the least misleading. Not in the glossary and worth adding, since the corpus contains material on the ruling concerning music.

translator_notes: A news-desk announcement posted on the day. It records that the lecture happened and gives nothing of its content.
The CMS timestamp, 3 July 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body gives the same day for the lecture.

Proper names follow the style guide's rule of standard romanisation without diacritics. Rached Ghannouchi and Salman al-Awdah are given in the forms usual in English; Muhammad Imarah and Abd al-Qadir Quzah are transliterated. The source misspells عمارة as عماره.
'فور شباب' is 4Shabab, a satellite channel and youth organisation; the numeral form is the one it uses itself.
